findings.text: Main executable text grouping defines a fixed order with function alignment first, page alignment before the hot portion, and dedicated trailing slots for main plus fixup, non-instrumentable and reference contributions alongside sanitizer, unclassified, split and unlikely contributions.

Specialized code groupings each align to function boundary and expose paired start and end markers bracketing one dedicated input class for scheduler, locking, probes, entry, interrupt entry, soft interrupt entry and static call code.

Early head code is retained unconditionally while its section carries explicit load address adjustment; fault fixup table is aligned on a caller-provided boundary and wrapped with paired table bounds under load offset adjustment.
Type information emission has two build configurations: one emitting page-aligned type and identifier groupings with bounds and load adjustment, another emitting nothing.

Initial task data placement honors caller alignment with load adjustment; constructor handling has two builds, one collecting sorted and unsorted constructor and init-array inputs between start and end markers with eight alignment, another empty.

Initialization and exit groupings separate data from code: init data aggregates entry, init data, constructors, tracing, probe, device-tree and firmware-table, security and test registration inputs; init text aggregates init and startup code; exit data aggregates exit data, finalizer and destructor inputs; exit text aggregates exit code; exit calls form a single dedicated input class.

Small and general uninitialized data handling aligns each output on caller size, applies load adjustment, and orders dynamic, main and common-like inputs, with general zero data page-aligning dedicated page-aligned and dynamic inputs and allowing an empty first-subsection hook.
Debug information is mapped to zero-address non-loadable outputs preserving standard DWARF version groupings and STABS groupings without contributing to the loadable image.

Live-patch symbol identifiers have emitting and empty builds; general object metadata collects comment, symbol, string and section-name inputs at zero address plus live-patch identifiers, while module information collects its dedicated input with trailing eight alignment.

Bug reporting table has emitting variant aligned to eight with bounded table and load adjustment and empty variant; unwind support has emitting variant with header, address and entry tables plus derived text-size-based lookup reservation bracketed by lookup bounds, and empty variant.

Built-in firmware, trace data and printk index outputs each have emitting and empty builds; emitting forms use load adjustment with eight or four alignment as appropriate and bounded sections exposing start and end markers for firmware and trace data.

Initialization calls progress through ordered levels from early through numbered stages with a distinct root filesystem stage between later numbers to a final end marker, each level retaining its dedicated init inputs between level start markers.

Notes discard stack and property notes and collect remaining notes with bounds and header handling; setup, console init, generically named, runtime-constant and unit-test helpers provide aligned bounded collections with start and end markers for parameters, consoles, named runtime values and test suites.

Initial RAM filesystem, decrypted per-CPU data and profile data each have emitting and empty builds; emitting forms use four-byte, page or unsized handling and retain dedicated inputs with start markers or page bracketing where applicable.

Discard handling drops exit code and data when configured, optionally drops exception-frame inputs, varies sanitizer-related discards across three builds, and always discards generic discard, symbol-trim, version and tracepoint-check inputs under a single discard output together with exit calls.

Per-CPU template layout defines ordered regions from page-aligned entries through cacheline-aligned hot sorted entries bracketed by hot bounds, read-mostly, general, shared-aligned and optionally decrypted entries, bracketed by overall start and end markers; section wrapper page-aligns the whole template with load adjustment.

Writable data, init text, init data and zero-data top-level sections apply page or caller alignment and load adjustment, expose init-text and zero-data boundary symbols, and nest task, power, alignment-sensitive, read-mostly, generic, constructor, bug-table, setup, call-level, console, RAM-filesystem and small plus general zero-data groupings in fixed order.
First word-scan descriptor holds two masking constants derived from repeated low-value and high-bit patterns for detecting zero bytes within a machine word.
Second word-scan descriptor holds unit and high-bit repeated patterns offering an alternative zero-byte detection parameterization.

Word-scan helpers expose operations to test a word for embedded zero bytes while saving intermediate state, derive a mask from that state, locate first zero position, expand a match into a trailing bytemask, and count masked bytes, with two alternative strategy families and word-size-sensitive counting.
Accounting interface defines version and tick-rate constants with three version builds and two tick-rate plus record-type pairings, selecting among legacy and newer record layouts.
Accounting collection, process accounting and namespace-exit hooks can collapse to operations that accept their arguments and do nothing.

Tick conversions translate between kernel ticks or nanoseconds and accounting ticks, using exact division or multiplication when rates divide evenly and wider intermediate arithmetic otherwise, including a scaled approximation path for unusual accounting rates.

Firmware companion helpers expose handle retrieval that tolerates missing devices, companion lookup and assignment, handle derivation from device or firmware node, static firmware-node allocation with initialization, static-node release guarded by type check, companion presence test, companion presetting from parent address lookup, dependency clearing, and device naming preferring init name before object name.

Companion support has enabled and disabled builds; disabled builds define companion lookup as null, companion assignment as inert, presence and node-type tests as false, while symbol export and init-section attributes likewise collapse or expand depending on library versus built-in configuration.
Headers use single-definition include guards ensuring idempotent inclusion.
Static firmware-node allocation can fail and report absence; release warns and returns early when given a non-static node rather than freeing.
